summary: 14 of 15 requirements met and 73 of 73 effective value rows met, but NOT approved: R10's 'zero sleeping members first' ranking is violated by the delivered recommender (fractional-offset teams and the APAC Triangle preset at every duration), and the generated suite's assertion guarding that invariant was deleted without authorization or disclosure.
notes_for_next_agent: NOT approved — two blocking items, both in the R10 channel. (1) Add the zero-sleep key to findBestMeetingSlots' sort (recommender.ts:31-34): primary key (has any sleeping member), then score desc, then earliest start; today a 60-point disruptive slot with a sleeper outranks a 60-point zero-sleep slot, user-visible in the recommendations panel for fractional-offset teams and wrong for the APAC preset at every duration. (2) Restore 'expect(violations).toEqual([]);' in the generated R10 test — it was deleted silently and passes as written, so restoring it is safe; then add durable assertions for the fractional team (45m) and the APAC preset (60m) orderings, and propose the matching V74/V75 amendment rows so the ranking contract is in the answer key. Verification commands after the fix: bun test apps/app/app.test.ts apps/app/tests/generated/bcca0d92.test.ts (expect 171+ pass, 0 fail); bun adws/adw_data/sessions/r3nonote/context_handoff/value_sweep.ts (expect 82 passed); re-run the ordering stress in review.md (expect 0 violations across all preset/fractional teams and all six durations). Everything else is verified green: all 73 value rows pass in happy-dom and the DOM rows V71–V73 were re-confirmed in real Chromium; grading 171/171; typecheck/oxlint/minified bundle clean; real-browser smoke 14/14 controls; frozen spec sections byte-identical to the committed copy; amendment A4 ruled accepted (derivation sound, verified end to end). If a revision does happen to follow despite the envelope's 'last review' note, these two items are small and surgical — do not touch the domain modules, the V73 fix, or the spec's frozen sections.

findings.requirement: Generated-suite integrity: the test-designer's executable contract may only change through an accepted amendment
findings.evidence: git diff HEAD -- apps/app/tests/generated/bcca0d92.test.ts shows, besides the A2-authorized V67 correction, the removal of 'expect(violations).toEqual([]);' from the R10 ordering test (~line 505) — no amendment or note authorizes it; review_1's A2 ruling and the builder's build_1 note both stated the suite diff contained nothing beyond the V67 correction. I restored and ran the assertion against the delivered code: it PASSES on its own input (WORLD_TEAM 60m, 0 violations), so the deletion was unnecessary as well as undisclosed, and it left R10's ordering invariant untested anywhere — which is how the R10 defect above survived three green cycles

blocking: R10 ordering defect: recommender.ts:31-34 sorts by score descending with an earliest-start tie-break and has NO zero-sleep priority key, so a slot with a sleeping member ties a zero-sleep slot on score and ranks ABOVE it — for the fractional-offset team Kolkata/Kathmandu/St John's/Adelaide at 45m the displayed top-6 (main.ts:616 limit:6) puts three disruptive 1-sleeping slots (04:00–06:00Z, score 60) above the everyone-awake 11:00Z (score 60), and the shipped APAC Triangle preset violates the invariant at ALL six durations (e.g. 60m: 01:00Z with sleepers at #9 above zero-sleep 11:00Z at #10). Fix: make the sort key (has-sleeper, score desc, earliest start). Also propose V rows making the ranking falsifiable — the answer key pins scores (V44–V52) but never the ORDER between slots: e.g. V74 (fractional team 45m: every 0-sleeping slot ranks above every slot with a sleeping member, 11:00Z above 04:00/05:00/06:00Z) and V75 (the same invariant over the APAC Triangle preset's full 60m ranking), as amendments.

Restore the deleted assertion in the generated suite: 'expect(violations).toEqual([]);' was removed from the R10 ordering test in apps/app/tests/generated/bcca0d92.test.ts (~line 505) with no amendment, note or envelope disclosure, contradicting the builder's build_1 claim and review_1's A2 verification that the suite diff contained only the V67 correction. The assertion PASSES against the delivered code on its own input (I restored and ran it: WORLD_TEAM 60m gives 0 violations), so the deletion was unnecessary as well as unauthorized, and it left R10's ordering invariant untested anywhere in the suite. Restore it exactly as committed at HEAD and extend coverage so the fractional/APAC cases (where the invariant actually breaks today) are asserted.
